key_insight: Putting trainable nonlinear functions on connections, rather than only on nodes, makes analogue neural networks especially efficient for smooth continuous-control tasks.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a low-power hardware path for robotic control and photovoltaic maximum-power-point tracking, with a projected CMOS power around 30 microwatts.
method: Implemented trainable nonlinear connections as analogue band-pass filters on field-programmable analogue arrays.
Compared performance on smooth regression/control tasks versus classification-like decision boundaries.
Also tested transfer to hardware and a memristive simulation to check device-agnostic behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantified fidelity when transferring trained networks across about 35,000 connections and shows far fewer nodes/connections than multilayer perceptrons on smooth targets.
watch_item: The advantage is task-dependent and does not appear for classification-like decision boundaries, so the architecture is not universally parameter-efficient.
paper_title: Low-power analogue neural networks with trainable nonlinear connections for continuous control
